reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Grading forehead movement in a central (upper motor neuron) facial palsy, where the forehead is often spared.
name: House-Brackmann Facial Nerve Grading System

version.label: House-Brackmann grading system, grades I–VI (House & Brackmann 1985)
version.detail: Six grades based on gross appearance, symmetry at rest and movement of forehead, eye and mouth. Later revisions (e.g. House-Brackmann 2.0, 2009) are different versions and are not combined.

purpose: Grades overall facial nerve function, for example after vestibular schwannoma surgery or Bell palsy.
intendedPopulation: Patients with peripheral facial nerve dysfunction.

calculatorNotice.title: Choose the best-fitting grade
calculatorNotice.message: When features fall between grades, choose the grade that best fits overall; eye closure is often the deciding feature.

options.label: I: Normal
options.detail: Normal facial function in all areas.

options.label: II: Mild dysfunction
options.detail: Slight weakness on close inspection; possibly very slight synkinesis. Normal symmetry and tone at rest. Forehead: moderate to good movement. Eye: complete closure with minimal effort. Mouth: slight asymmetry.

options.label: III: Moderate dysfunction
options.detail: Obvious but not disfiguring difference between sides; noticeable but not severe synkinesis, contracture or hemifacial spasm. Normal symmetry and tone at rest. Forehead: slight to moderate movement. Eye: complete closure with effort. Mouth: slightly weak with maximum effort.

options.label: IV: Moderately severe dysfunction
options.detail: Obvious weakness and/or disfiguring asymmetry. Normal symmetry and tone at rest. Forehead: no movement. Eye: incomplete closure. Mouth: asymmetric with maximum effort.

options.label: V: Severe dysfunction
options.detail: Only barely perceptible movement. Asymmetry at rest. Forehead: no movement. Eye: incomplete closure. Mouth: slight movement.

inputDefinitions.label: Side (optional)
inputDefinitions.help: Recorded for the share text only; it does not change the grade.

resultStates.label: Grade I: normal
resultStates.summary: Normal facial function in all areas at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Describes facial movement at this timepoint; delayed weakness can occur after surgery.

resultStates.label: Grade II: mild dysfunction
resultStates.summary: Slight weakness on close inspection; possibly very slight synkinesis. Normal symmetry and tone at rest. Forehead: moderate to good movement. Eye: complete closure with minimal effort. Mouth: slight asymmetry.

resultStates.label: Grade III: moderate dysfunction
resultStates.summary: Obvious but not disfiguring difference between sides; noticeable but not severe synkinesis, contracture or hemifacial spasm. Normal symmetry and tone at rest. Forehead: slight to moderate movement. Eye: complete closure with effort. Mouth: slightly weak with maximum effort.

resultStates.label: Grade IV: moderately severe dysfunction
resultStates.summary: Obvious weakness and/or disfiguring asymmetry. Normal symmetry and tone at rest. Forehead: no movement. Eye: incomplete closure. Mouth: asymmetric with maximum effort.

resultStates.label: Grade V: severe dysfunction
resultStates.summary: Only barely perceptible movement. Asymmetry at rest. Forehead: no movement. Eye: incomplete closure. Mouth: slight movement.
resultStates.detail: Assess eye closure and corneal protection according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

resultStates.label: Grade VI: total paralysis
resultStates.detail: Assess eye closure and corneal protection according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: The most widely used grading of facial nerve function.
Complete eye closure separates grade III from grade IV.

clinicalInsights.text: Incomplete eye closure (grades IV–VI): corneal exposure is a risk to assess.
Record the timepoint (e.g. preoperative, day 1, 1 year), as recovery changes the grade.

limitations.text: A single global grade; regional differences (e.g. good eye closure but weak mouth) are not captured.

limitations: Synkinesis and secondary changes are not graded separately.
Inter-rater agreement is lower for intermediate grades (III–IV).

confounders.factor: Prior facial surgery or eyelid procedures

confounders.effect: Removes the normal side for comparison.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The cause or site of the facial nerve lesion.

guideSections.what: A six-grade scale (I normal to VI total paralysis) of facial nerve function.
guideSections.whenToUse: Before and after cerebellopontine angle and skull base surgery; Bell palsy and other peripheral facial palsies.
guideSections.howToPerform: Observe the face at rest, then ask the patient to raise the eyebrows, close the eyes gently and tightly, and smile. Compare sides and choose the grade that best fits.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Designed for peripheral facial nerve dysfunction; forehead sparing suggests a central cause.

sources.citation: House JW, Brackmann DE. Facial nerve grading system. Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 1985;93(2):146-147.
